cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to Timothy, his true child in the faith. Paul has urged Timothy to stay on at Ephesus and stop certain men from teaching false doctrines. Big job. Paul's not done talking, though.
Then Paul stops right there and says thank you to Christ Jesus our Lord, who has strengthened him. Mid-letter. No warning. Just GRATITUDE.

cards.question: Paul thanks Jesus for appointing him to service, because Jesus considered him ___.

cards.text: Before all this, Paul was a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man. Friend, that's not a résumé. That's a WARNING LABEL.

cards.question: Paul used to be a blasphemer, a persecutor and a violent man. What does he say he was shown?
Paul says that back when he was a persecutor, he knew full well what he was doing.

cards.text: And it doesn't stop at mercy. The grace of our Lord OVERFLOWED to Paul, like the day the lid popped off my sprinkle jar, except this was on purpose.

cards.question: Grace overflowed to Paul. What came right along with it, found in Christ Jesus?

cards.text: Then Paul shares a saying he calls trustworthy and worthy of full acceptance. Lean in, friend. This one's the whole recipe.

cards.question: What's the trustworthy saying Paul shares with Timothy?

answers.text: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners
Christ Jesus came into the world to reward the good
Christ Jesus came into the world to rebuild the temple

cards.question: Christ Jesus came to save sinners, and Paul says that of those sinners, he is the ___.

cards.text: Most folks fight for first place, and Paul's over here claiming the crumbs at the bottom of the box. So why would Jesus show mercy to the worst of sinners?

cards.question: Why does Paul say he, the worst of sinners, was shown mercy?

answers.text: So Jesus could display His patience as an example
Because Paul had earned it by keeping the law
Because the apostles in Jerusalem asked for it

cards.question: Paul says Jesus showed him just a little patience, enough to get by.

cards.text: Right there in the letter, Paul bursts into praise, like me when the timer dings on a perfect batch, only a WHOLE lot holier. He gives honor and glory forever and ever to the King, the only God. Amen.

cards.question: Paul says the King he's praising will reign for a while and then pass away.

cards.text: Now Paul turns to Timothy and calls him his child. He entrusts him with a command, in keeping with the previous prophecies about him.

cards.question: Paul's command lines up with the prophecies about Timothy. What are those prophecies meant to help Timothy do?

cards.text: Now, the biggest fight I've ever been in was with a stubborn ball of dough. And I LOST. But Paul tells Timothy exactly how to fight this one.

cards.question: How does Paul tell Timothy to fight the good fight?

answers.text: By holding on to faith and a good conscience
By holding on to the law and the temple
By holding on to his rights and his reputation

cards.question: Paul says some have rejected faith and a good conscience, and so they have ___ their faith.

cards.text: Shipwrecked faith, friend. I once flipped a whole tray of cookies face-down on the floor, and even I can tell this is worse.

cards.question: Paul names two men among those who shipwrecked their faith. Who are they?
Paul says he handed Hymenaeus and Alexander over to Satan so they would be taught not to blaspheme.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Paul, an apostle… faith.' 'Paul has urged… doctrines.' 'Big job.' 'Paul's not done talking, though.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: This story card has 4 sentences: the thanks, then 'Mid-letter.' 'No warning.' 'Just GRATITUDE.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus appointed Paul to service 'because' He considered him faithful. The BSB says only 'that He considered me faithful and appointed me to service.' The text joins the two with 'and' and leaves the connection open. The card adds a cause.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Before all this… violent man.' 'Friend, that's not a résumé.' 'That's a WARNING LABEL.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Peace and quiet' is a casual modern idiom. 'Faith and love' and 'Riches and honor' sound like Bible pairs. Because the wrong answer is in a different register, the answers don't sound alike.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Then Paul shares a saying…' 'Lean in, friend.' 'This one's the whole recipe.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. Its first sentence is a joke restating card 11's answer (Paul is the worst of sinners). Its second sentence only sets up the question. It cites 1 Timothy 1:15 but carries no new part of that verse. It works as a recap and a reaction, not as a new piece of the passage with a joke riding along.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The end of 1 Timothy 1:16 is never told or asked. Paul says his mercy is an example 'to those who would believe in Him for eternal life.' Card 13 stops at 'as an example', and no card says who it is an example for or mentions eternal life.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Right there in the letter… holier.' 'He gives honor and glory… only God.' 'Amen.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'He gives honor and glory forever and ever to the King' changes the form of 1 Timothy 1:17. The verse is a doxology: 'Now to the King… be honor and glory forever and ever.' Paul declares that honor and glory be to God. He is not described as giving them.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Card 1 just told the baker that honor and glory go to this King 'forever and ever' and that He is 'the only God.' That rules out card 2's statement that the King 'will reign for a while and then pass away,' so the setup gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Now, the biggest fight… dough.' 'And I LOST.' 'But Paul tells Timothy…'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats card 7's answer ('Shipwrecked faith') and adds a joke. It cites 1 Timothy 1:19 but no new part of that verse.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
